statutes.shortName: Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Ordinance No. 13 of 1907

sections.title: Cruelty, Beating, Overloading, and Improper Transport
sections.offence: Cruelly beating, ill-treating, overloading, torturing, or transporting any animal in a manner causing unnecessary pain.
sections.penalty: Fine up to Rs. 100 or imprisonment up to 3 months (simple or rigorous) or both.

sections.title: Starvation and Severe Neglect
sections.offence: Allowing an animal to suffer from starvation, mutilation, or serious neglect.
sections.penalty: Fine up to Rs. 100 (repeat offence: up to Rs. 200 or 3 months imprisonment).

sections.title: Cruel Killing
sections.offence: Killing an animal in an unnecessarily cruel manner.
sections.penalty: Fine up to Rs. 100 and/or imprisonment up to 6 months.

sections.title: Working Unfit or Diseased Animals
sections.offence: Working or employing any animal unfit for work due to wound, disease, or exhaustion.
sections.penalty: Fine up to Rs. 100 and/or imprisonment up to 6 months.

sections.title: Abandonment on Streets
sections.offence: Abandoning diseased or disabled animals on public roads or streets to die.
sections.penalty: Fine up to Rs. 100 or imprisonment up to 3 months.

sections.title: Statute of Limitations (3 Months)
sections.rule: Every prosecution must be instituted within THREE MONTHS from the date of the offence.

sections.title: Cognizable Offence (Arrest Without Warrant)
sections.power: All offences under this Ordinance are cognizable. Police officers may arrest offenders without a warrant.

statutes.shortName: Animals Act No. 29 of 1958 & Gazette No. 1629/17 (2009)

sections.title: Mandatory Ear Tags & Cattle Vouchers
sections.requirement: All cattle/buffalo over 18 months must carry ear tags and a Cattle Voucher (Schedule 06) signed before the GVS.

sections.title: Mandatory Livestock Transport Documents
sections.requirement: Requires DS Transport Permit (Sched 01), GVS Health Cert (Sched 03), Vehicle Fitness Cert (Sched 04 & 05), loading ramp, and 30x4 inch red-on-white signboard.

sections.title: 2026 Expansion to Small Ruminants & Pigs
sections.requirement: Extends Part II mandatory transport permits, vehicle inspection, and movement tracking to goats, sheep, and pigs.

sections.title: Mandatory Butcher Licensing
sections.requirement: Annual license required from Municipal Mayor or Local Council Chairman. Unlicensed butchery carries fines up to Rs. 20,000.

sections.title: Absolute Ban on Slaughter of Pregnant or Lactating Cows
sections.penalty: Mandatory fine of Rs. 50,000 and imprisonment up to 3 years.

statutes.shortName: Dangerous Animals Ordinance No. 38 of 1921 (Amended by Act No. 40 of 2022)

sections.title: Negligent Control of Ferocious Animals
sections.penalty: Penalty raised in Nov 2022 from Rs. 1,000 to Rs. 250,000.

statutes.shortName: Fauna and Flora Protection Ordinance No. 2 of 1937 (FFPO)

sections.title: Protection of Elephants and Tamed Elephant Registration
sections.requirement: Strict protection of wild elephants. Mandatory DWC registration for captive elephants.

sections.title: Negligent Handling of Animals Endangering Humans
sections.penalty: Imprisonment up to 6 months and/or fine.

sections.title: Mischief by Killing or Maiming Animals (Valued Rs. 10+)
sections.penalty: Imprisonment up to 2 years and/or fine.

sections.title: Mischief by Killing or Maiming Cattle, Horses, Elephants
sections.penalty: Imprisonment up to 5 years and/or fine.

sections.title: Statutory Duty of Care
sections.description: Obliges animal custodians to meet essential welfare needs (nutrition, environment, healthcare, normal behavior).

sections.title: Substantially Increased Sanctions
sections.penalty: Fines up to Rs. 500,000 and imprisonment up to 3 years.

sections.title: National Animal Welfare Authority & 20 Regulated Fields
sections.description: Establishes NAWA and regulates commercial breeding, pet shops, fighting, and transport.

caseLaws.principle: Captive wild animals (such as a captured Dugong) are legally protected as 'animals' under the 1907 Cruelty Ordinance.
Vicarious liability: Master/owner has an absolute duty of active supervision over working animals; oral orders to carters do not excuse liability.

caseLaws.citation: Inspector SPCA Nawalapitiya v. Punchirala (1921) 24 NLR 202
caseLaws.principle: Beating a cornered wild elk with clubs constitutes illegal cruelty under Section 2 of Ordinance No. 13 of 1907.
Shooting a trespassing cow on private land causes unnecessary pain and is a punishable criminal offence under Section 4(1)(b).
Courts possess legal power to confiscate vehicles used for illegal cattle transport.
Magistrates may grant temporary care and custody of cruelty victims to recognized animal welfare organizations on a bond pending trial.

caseLaws.caseName: Justice for Animals and Nature v. OIC Udawalawa Police
caseLaws.principle: Magistrate order releasing cruelly transported buffaloes back to convicted perpetrators is illegal and set aside.

caseLaws.caseName: Irangani De Silva v. OIC Ella
caseLaws.principle: Cattle vouchers required to prove lawful ownership; animal welfare societies have recognized locus standi to intervene in court.
